newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Gains to Slovnaft shares drive Slovak BSE higher.
newsitem.headline: Gains to Slovnaft shares drive Slovak BSE higher.

text.p: Slovak blue chips were mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchande (BSE) on Thursday, with brokers predicting an increase in foreign demand to spur the bourse on a long-term uptrend.
Slovnaft, the market's largest issue, gained 30 crowns to close at 830 and push the SAX index up 3.07 points to 189.40.
"Demand is now higher than supply and a surge on the Czech market should bring more foreign investors to Slovakia as well and push the bourse further up," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.

Oil and gas storage firm Nafta continued to attract little interest due to uncertanity over the future strategy of its owners, but brokers said the overall bullish sentiment would push its price higher. Nafta traded only 22 shares today, closing up 10 crowns at 1,700.
Steel maker VSZ closed unchanged at 660, and brokers said the share, one of the most liquid on the BSE, had the potential to rise in the near future.
Overall volume fell to 154,397 shares from 266,926 stocks traded on Wednesday. Turnover was down to 60.75 million crowns from 148.14 million on Wednesday.
